title: 第126章剑心无杂念第125章深山隐正道
content_zh:
苍梧山脉连绵千里，层峦叠嶂，常年被浓稠的墨色云雾笼罩。山间古木参天，虬枝交错，遮断天光，谷底阴风穿林而过，卷着细碎的水雾与腐叶气息，终年不散。青龙潭便隐匿在苍梧山最幽深的绝境之中，是世间少有的阴寒剑修秘境，也是无数剑道修士又爱又惧的磨砺之地。传闻此潭上古有神龙蛰伏，死后残魂凝聚潭底，千年阴气淬炼潭水，暗藏剑道大道，可洗练剑心、淬养剑意，却也能吞噬杂念、绞碎心神，但凡心怀虚妄、执念深重之人踏入此地，轻则道心受损、剑意溃散，重则神魂沉沦、永坠渊底。
萧琰立在青龙潭崖边，白衣素净，不染半点尘霜。
山风烈烈，吹得他衣袂翻飞，墨色长发肆意飘舞，却吹不动他眼底半分波澜。少年身姿挺拔如青松立崖，脊背笔直，肩腰舒展，一柄朴素无华的青锋长剑斜负身后，剑鞘是寻常青木所制，无金玉纹饰，无宗门徽记，平平无奇，却隐隐透出一缕沉稳内敛的锋锐。他今年十七岁，历经江湖恩怨、宗门纷争，身负未解的身世羁绊，也曾被情仇裹挟、被俗世牵绊，可此刻立于绝境潭边，过往种种浮沉皆尽数沉淀，不留半分躁动。
世人皆道，剑道之路，需执念炽热，需杀伐果决，需一心求胜、步步争先，方能登临绝顶，勘破无上剑道。可萧琰一路走来，见惯了执剑者的癫狂与虚妄。有人执着于门派排名，终生争名逐利，最终剑心蒙尘，修为停滞；有人执念于复仇血海，剑意暴戾偏激，最终走火入魔，自毁道途；有人贪恋修为境界，急于求成，反而根基虚浮，难窥大道真意。
唯有他渐渐悟得，真正的剑道，从不是偏执强求，而是剑心无杂念，方寸守清明。
此番前来青龙潭，他并非为争夺秘境机缘，不是为求取绝世修为，更不是为一战成名、震慑江湖。他只是为洗炼本心，磨尽最后一丝残留的俗世杂念，让自己的剑、自己的心，彻底归于纯粹，归于本真。
崖下青龙潭，潭水漆黑如墨，静谧得没有一丝涟漪。寻常深潭必有水声潺潺、鱼跃波涌，可这片潭水死寂得诡异，仿佛连风都不敢惊扰这片渊底沉寂。潭面之上萦绕着层层淡青色阴雾，雾气冰凉刺骨，裹挟着浓郁的剑道威压，沉沉压在人心神之上。雾气之中，隐约流转着细碎的银色剑光，那是千年潭水吸纳天地剑气、蕴养大道法理凝聚而成的剑意残丝，无形无质，却锋利至极，可勘破一切虚妄，照见人心深处所有杂念与贪痴。
无数顶尖剑修曾慕名而来，欲借青龙潭之力突破桎梏、凝练无上剑意，可大多人皆是乘兴而来，败兴而归，更有甚者，自此销声匿迹，尸骨无存。究其根本，便是人心杂念丛生，贪念、执念、嗔念、痴念缠绕于心，一旦入潭，潭中剑意便会无限放大心底所有晦暗，让人自困心魔、自我瓦解。
萧琰抬眸，目光平静地扫过整片青龙潭域。
他的眼眸澄澈如寒潭净水，无贪、无惧、无喜、无悲。身后青锋长剑微微震颤，发出一声细微的嗡鸣，不是躁动不安，而是共鸣契合，似是知晓主人心意，已然做好了静心悟道、淬炼本心的准备。
旁人入此秘境，必先凝神戒备，运转全身修为抵御阴寒威压，小心翼翼探查周遭风险，唯恐被心魔侵扰、被剑意所伤。可萧琰未曾运转半分灵力护体，就这般步履从容，一步步踏下陡峭湿滑的崖壁，朝着潭边缓步走去。
脚下青石常年被潭水雾气浸润，湿滑冰凉，布满细碎的青苔，稍有不慎便会失足坠渊。山间阴风卷着刺骨寒气扑面而来，侵入肌骨，寻常修士在此片刻便会气血凝滞、心神紧绷，可萧琰步履沉稳，步伐不急不缓，每一步落地都安稳笃定，心神始终保持极致的平静。
杂念者，方寸之乱，道心之障。
萧琰心中了然，过往数年修行，他也曾有过迷茫，有过焦灼。初入剑道时，他急于精进修为，日夜苦修，执念于突破境界；身负身世谜团时，他曾被恩怨牵绊，心绪难平，剑势之中带着几分戾气；目睹江湖纷争、正邪混战，他也曾动过恻隐、生过愤慨，心绪起伏不定。这些细碎的情绪，看似微不足道，实则都是剑道路上的桎梏，是藏在心底的杂念，悄然遮蔽着剑道本心。
而今日青龙潭一行，便是他斩断杂念、纯粹剑心的最后一关。
行至潭边，冰凉的潭风扑面而来，雾气缠绕周身，瞬间浸透衣衫，贴在肌肤之上，寒意彻骨。潭中沉寂的漆黑水面仿佛一面巨大的魔镜，沉沉倒映着他的身影，却又模糊扭曲，看不真切。隐约之间，潭底深处传来幽幽低鸣，似龙吟余响，又似万千剑鸣交织，低沉悠远，回荡在整个山谷之间，震得空气微微震颤。
这是青龙潭的心境幻音，专扰人心神。修为越高、执念越重之人，听闻此音，心境波动便会越剧烈，极易陷入自身执念幻境，永世沉沦。
萧琰静静伫立潭边，双目微阖，凝神静气。
低鸣入耳，他的心底没有掀起丝毫波澜。那些曾经让他辗转难眠的恩怨、让他急于求成的执念、让他心绪起伏的得失，在此刻尽数如烟消散。他不追巅峰，不惧绝境，不念过往，不忧未来，心中唯有一剑，唯守一心。
片刻之后，他缓缓抬手，握住了身后的青锋剑柄。

指尖触碰到微凉的剑鞘，熟悉的触感顺着指尖蔓延全身，瞬间抚平了心底最后一丝微不可察的躁动。人与剑相伴数载，早已心意相通，剑是心之载体，心是剑之根本。心有杂念，则剑势浮躁凌厉，失之沉稳；心无杂念，则剑势澄澈通透，直指大道。
“今日，借青龙潭一剑，洗尽尘心，永断杂念。”
萧琰轻声开口，嗓音清冽平稳，无半分波澜，不似立誓明志，更似喃喃自语，与天地大道轻声契合。
铮——
清越剑鸣骤然响彻山谷，刺破山间浓雾。青锋长剑脱鞘而出，不携半分杀伐戾气，不逞丝毫凌厉锋芒，凌空一转，稳稳悬于萧琰身前三尺之处。剑身莹白透亮，流转着温润的淡光，没有惊天动地的威势，却有着一种极致纯粹、返璞归真的大道气韵。
寻常修士拔剑，必带灵力震荡、气势磅礴，欲展己身锋芒，慑服四方。可萧琰这一剑，平淡、从容、澄澈、无争。
剑无争，故天下莫能与之争；心无杂，故世间无物可扰之。
萧琰抬步，踏入冰冷的潭水之中。
微凉刺骨的潭水没过脚踝，再漫过膝头，漆黑的水流缠绕四肢，带着极强的侵蚀之力与心神拉扯之力，试图侵入他的经脉、扰乱他的识海。潭底潜藏的万千剑意丝丝缕缕缠绕而来，如同无数细密丝线，试图勾动他心底的隐秘情绪，放大他过往的所有执念与遗憾。
刹那间，无数幻象在识海之中悄然浮现。
他看见年少时孤身练剑、屡屡受挫的焦灼，看见师门纷争中人心险恶的寒心，看见血海恩怨里身不由己的无奈，看见自己曾执着于变强、执着于真相、执着于善恶对错的偏执模样。一幕幕画面清晰真切，如同昨日重现，不断冲击着他的心神，试图勾起他的不甘、遗憾、愤怒与迷茫。
这便是青龙潭最恐怖的磨砺，不伤人肉身，只磨人心神。
心魔从不是外来妖魔，而是人心深处沉淀的杂念与执念。
无数剑修陨于此地，皆是因为在幻境之中难以自持，沉溺过往、困于得失，最终道心崩塌、剑意溃散，被潭水阴气吞噬，神魂俱灭。
可萧琰只是静静立在潭水中央，任由幻象翻涌、阴气侵蚀、剑意缠绕，心神始终澄澈通透，不起丝毫涟漪。
他看着识海中浮沉的过往，不眷恋、不悔恨、不愤慨、不纠结。年少焦灼，是成长必经之路，无需执念；人心险恶，是世间常态，无需介怀；身不由己，是俗世羁绊，无需沉溺。修行之路，本就是一路舍弃、一路沉淀、一路纯粹，若被过往牵绊、被得失束缚，便永远无法抵达剑道真境。
“过往皆序章，浮沉皆历练。”
萧琰低语一声，眸光愈发澄澈，“我剑只求纯粹，我心只求无杂，万般虚妄，皆可破。”
一语落罢，识海之中翻涌的幻象骤然一滞，随即如潮水般尽数褪去，不留半点痕迹。那些缠绕心神的杂念、牵绊道心的桎梏，在极致的清明本心面前，不堪一击，烟消云散。
content_en:
The Cangwu Mountains stretch for thousands of miles, with many mountains and mountains, and are shrouded in thick ink-colored clouds all year round. The ancient trees in the mountains are towering, and their branches are intertwined, blocking the skylight. The dark wind at the bottom of the valley passes through the forest, carrying fine mist and the smell of rotten leaves, which lingers all year round. Qinglongtan is hidden in the deepest desperate situation of Cangwu Mountain. It is a rare secret place for sword cultivation in the world, and it is also a training place that countless swordsmen monks love and fear. It is said that there was a divine dragon dormant in this pool in ancient times, and the remaining souls after death gathered at the bottom of the pool. Thousands of years of Yin Qi tempered the pool water, hiding the path of swordsmanship.
Xiao Yan stood on the edge of the Qinglong Pond, wearing pure white clothes and not stained by any dust or frost.
The mountain wind was so strong that it caused his clothes to fly and his long black hair to flutter wildly, but it couldn't make any waves in his eyes. The young man's posture is as tall as a green pine standing on a cliff, with a straight back, shoulders and waist stretched, and a simple green-edged long sword slanted behind his back. The scabbard is made of ordinary green wood, with no gold and jade decorations or sect emblems. It is unremarkable, but there is a faint hint of calm and restrained sharpness. He is seventeen years old this year. He has experienced grievances and sect disputes, and has been burdened with unresolved life experiences. He has also been entangled in love and hatred, and was bound by the world. But now he is standing on the edge of a pool of despair. All the ups and downs in the past have been settled, leaving no trace of restlessness.
Everyone knows that the road to swordsmanship requires ardent obsession, decisiveness in killing, a single-minded pursuit of victory, and striving for the lead step by step, in order to reach the top and explore the supreme swordsmanship. But along the way, Xiao Yan was used to seeing the madness and delusion of sword holders. Some people are obsessed with ranking in the sect, striving for fame and fortune all their lives, and eventually their swordsmanship becomes dusty and their cultivation becomes stagnant; some people are obsessed with revenge on the sea of ​​blood, and their swordsmanship becomes violent and extreme, and eventually they go crazy and destroy their own path; some people are greedy for the realm of cultivation and are eager to achieve success, but their foundation is empty and it is difficult to see the true meaning of the great path.
Only he gradually realized that the true way of swordsmanship is never paranoid and forceful, but a sword with no distracting thoughts and a clear mind.
He came to Qinglong Pond this time not to compete for opportunities in the secret realm, not to seek peerless cultivation, nor to become famous and shock the world in one battle. He just wanted to purify his true heart, grind away the last remaining worldly distractions, and make his sword and his heart completely pure and true.
At the foot of the cliff is the Qinglong Pool. The water in the pool is as dark as ink and so quiet that there is no ripple. Ordinary deep pools are bound to have the sound of gurgling water and leaping fish in the waves, but the water in this pool is eerily silent, as if not even the wind dares to disturb the silence at the bottom of the abyss. Layers of light cyan mist lingered above the surface of the pool. The mist was cold and biting, carrying a strong pressure from the sword, weighing heavily on people's minds. In the mist, there was faint silvery sword light flowing. It was the remnants of the sword intention condensed by the thousand-year-old pond water absorbing the sword energy of heaven and earth and cultivating the principles of the Tao. It was invisible and qualityless, but extremely sharp. It could detect all illusions and illuminate all the distracting thoughts and greed deep in the human heart.
Countless top sword cultivators have come here in admiration, hoping to use the power of Qinglong Pond to break through the shackles and condense the supreme sword intention. However, most of them came here in good spirits and returned in despair. What's worse, they have disappeared since then, with no remains of their bodies. The root cause is that the human heart is full of distracting thoughts, with greed, obsession, anger, and obsession entangled in the heart. Once entering the pool, the sword intention in the pool will infinitely amplify all the darkness in the heart, causing people to trap their own inner demons and self-disintegrate.
Xiao Yan raised his eyes and scanned the entire Qinglongtan area calmly.
His eyes are as clear as the pure water of a cold pool, without greed, fear, joy, or sorrow. The Qingfeng sword behind him trembled slightly and made a subtle hum. It was not restless, but a resonance. It seemed that he knew the master's intention and was ready to meditate on enlightenment and temper his heart.
When others enter this secret realm, they must first be alert, use their whole body's cultivation to resist the cold pressure, and carefully explore the dangers around them, lest they be invaded by inner demons and injured by the sword. But Xiao Yan neverUsing half of his spiritual power to protect his body, he walked calmly like this, stepping down the steep and slippery cliff step by step, and walked slowly towards the edge of the pool.
The bluestone under your feet has been soaked by the mist of the pool water all year round. It is wet and ice-cold, and covered with fine moss. If you are not careful, you will slip and fall into the abyss. The cold wind from the mountains blew towards the face and invaded the muscles and bones. Ordinary monks would have stagnant blood and tense mind at this moment, but Xiao Yan walked calmly, neither hastily nor slowly. Every step landed steadily and his mind always remained extremely calm.
Distracted thoughts lead to confusion and obstacles to the Taoist mind.
Xiao Yan knew clearly in his heart that in the past few years of practice, he had been confused and anxious. When he first entered the swordsmanship, he was eager to improve his cultivation, practiced hard day and night, and was obsessed with breaking through the realm; when he was faced with the mystery of his life experience, he was bound by grievances, and his mood was difficult to calm down, and his sword power contained a bit of violence; witnessing the disputes in the world and the melee between good and evil, he also felt compassion and indignation, and his mood fluctuated. These trivial emotions may seem insignificant, but in fact they are shackles on the path of swordsmanship. They are distracting thoughts hidden in the heart, quietly covering the true heart of swordsmanship.
Today's trip to Qinglongtan was the last step for him to cut off distracting thoughts and pure his sword heart.
Walking to the edge of the pool, the cold pool wind blew into my face, and the mist wrapped around my body, instantly soaking through my clothes and sticking to my skin, chilling me to the bone. The silent, dark water in the pool was like a huge magic mirror, reflecting his figure heavily, but it was blurry and distorted, making it difficult to see clearly. Indistinctly, a faint low roar came from the depths of the pool, like the lingering sound of a dragon's roar, or like the interweaving of thousands of swords. It was low and distant, echoing throughout the valley, making the air tremble slightly.
This is the phantom sound of Qinglongtan's state of mind, which is designed to disturb people's minds. The higher the level of cultivation and the more serious the obsession, the more violent the mood fluctuation will be when hearing this sound, and it is easy to fall into the illusion of one's own obsession and sink forever.
Xiao Yan stood quietly by the pool, eyes slightly closed, concentrating.
The low sound reached his ears, but it didn't stir up the slightest emotion in his heart. The grievances that once kept him awake, the obsession that made him eager for success, and the gains and losses that made him emotionally ups and downs all disappeared at this moment. He does not chase the peak, is not afraid of desperate situations, does not dwell on the past, and does not worry about the future. He only has one sword in his heart and only one mind.
After a moment, he slowly raised his hand and grasped the hilt of the Qingfeng sword behind him.
His fingertips touched the cool scabbard, and the familiar touch spread all over his body along his fingertips, instantly soothing the last trace of undetectable restlessness in his heart. People and swords have been together for several years, and their minds have long been connected. The sword is the carrier of the heart, and the heart is the root of the sword. If there are distracting thoughts in the mind, the sword force will be impetuous and sharp, and it will lose its composure; if there are no distracting thoughts in the mind, the sword force will be clear and transparent, pointing straight to the avenue.
"Today, I will borrow a sword from Qinglongtan to wash away all the dust in my heart and put an end to distracting thoughts forever."
Xiao Yan spoke softly, his voice clear and steady, without any waves. It didn't sound like he was making a vow, but more like he was mumbling to himself, softly in tune with the great road of heaven and earth.
Zheng——
The sound of Qingyue's sword suddenly resounded through the valley, piercing the dense fog in the mountains. The Qingfeng sword came out of its sheath, without any killing ferocity or sharp edge. It turned in the air and hung steadily three feet in front of Xiao Yan. The sword body is white and translucent, flowing with a gentle light. It does not have earth-shattering power, but it has an extremely pure and returning to nature aura.
When an ordinary monk draws his sword, it will bring about a shock of spiritual power and a majestic momentum, hoping to show off his own edge and overwhelm all parties. But Xiao Yan's sword was plain, calm, clear, and uncontested.
The sword has no dispute, so no one in the world can compete with it; the heart has no confusion, so nothing in the world can disturb it.
Xiao Yan stepped forward and stepped into the cold pool water.
The cold and biting water reached his ankles and then over his knees. The dark water wrapped around his limbs, bringing with it a strong corrosive force and a tugging force on his mind, trying to invade his meridians and disturb his sea of ​​consciousness. Thousands of sword intentions hidden at the bottom of the pool were entangled, like countless fine threads, trying to arouse the secret emotions in his heart and amplify all his past obsessions.and regret.
In an instant, countless illusions quietly emerged in the sea of ​​consciousness.
He saw the anxiety of practicing sword fighting alone when he was young and suffered repeated setbacks; he saw the sinister coldness of people in the disputes between masters; he saw the helplessness of being unable to control himself in the sea of ​​blood and grudges; he saw his paranoid appearance of being obsessed with becoming stronger, obsessed with the truth, and obsessed with good and evil, right and wrong. The scenes were clear and vivid, as if they were reappearing yesterday, constantly impacting his mind, trying to evoke his unwillingness, regret, anger and confusion.
This is the most terrifying test in Qinglongtan. It does not hurt the body, but only hurts the mind.
Inner demons are never external demons, but the distracting thoughts and obsessions deep in the human heart.
Countless sword cultivators died here because they were unable to control themselves in the illusion, indulged in the past, and trapped in gains and losses. In the end, their Taoist heart collapsed, their sword intent collapsed, and they were swallowed up by the Yin Qi of the pond, and their souls were destroyed.
But Xiao Yan just stood quietly in the middle of the pool, letting the illusions surge, the Yin Qi corrode, and the sword intent entangled, and his mind was always clear and transparent without any ripples.
He looked at the past floating in the sea of ​​consciousness without nostalgia, regret, anger, or entanglement. Anxiety at a young age is the only way to grow up, and there is no need for obsession; the human heart is sinister, which is the normal state of the world, and there is no need to care about it; the inability to control oneself is the fetters of the world, and there is no need to indulge in it. The path of spiritual practice is to give up, settle, and be pure all the way. If you are hampered by the past and bound by gains and losses, you will never reach the true realm of swordsmanship.
"The past is a prologue, and the ups and downs are all experiences."
Xiao Yan whispered, his eyes becoming clearer, "My sword only seeks purity, and my heart only seeks purity. It can break all kinds of illusions."
As soon as he finished speaking, the illusions surging in the sea of consciousness suddenly stagnated, and then they all faded away like the tide, leaving no trace. Those distracting thoughts that entangle the mind and the shackles that hinder the Taoist heart are vulnerable to a blow and disappear in the face of the ultimate clear mind.
